name: Haiku dividend growth and income
strategy: Core dividend aristocrats (JNJ, PG, KO, MCD, ABT, MMM) provide capital preservation and stable income; tactical overweight to energy (XLE) capitalizing on geopolitical oil supply support; TLT short hedge against rising rates; elevated cash (39.5%) for 4% APY income and optionality.
reassessment_note: Previous thesis on small-cap recovery (IWM +0.71% since entry) and semiconductor consolidation (SOXL +3.98% entry bounce but -32% over 2-week horizon) has failed. Rising bond yields (10-year at 4.79%, highest since Jan 2025) driven by geopolitical tensions (US-Iran Strait conflict) and strong employment data have triggered Fed hike probability to 66% for Sept 18. Leverage positions (UPRO, SOXL) are increasingly vulnerable to rate shocks and beta decay. Market rotating from growth/leverage to value (VTV +7.2% outperformance YTD). Repositioning to high-quality dividend aristocrats with 60+ year track records, offering capital preservation and dividend growth through rising rate cycles. Tactical energy tilt (XLE +7.57%) captures geopolitical tailwind for oil dividends. TLT short provides direct rate hedge. Elevated cash (39.5%) at 4% APY is income diversification and maintains dry powder for opportunities post-hike volatility.

positions.thesis: Healthcare dividend aristocrat with 61 consecutive years of dividend increases. Best-in-class pharma portfolio, pricing power, and defensive characteristics. Current 3.53% YTD performance in my entry (275.23) reflects resilience. Provides stable cash flow and capital preservation in rising rate environment.

Consumer staples dividend aristocrat with 68 consecutive years of increases. Pricing power in consumer staples maintains margins through inflation. Brand moat (Gillette, Olay, Tide) and defensive positioning. Recent entry at 146.44 (up 0.91% since entry) shows stability. Income generation through cycles.

Beverage dividend aristocrat with 61 years of consecutive increases and highest dividend yield among core holdings (3.0%+ yield). Pricing power, global distribution, and recession-resistant demand. Provides yield while holding through rate volatility. Diversifies sector exposure vs healthcare/staples concentration.

Dividend aristocrat with 50+ year track record. Franchisee model provides recurring revenue and cash flow stability. Currently down -2.29% (255.69) but fundamentals support recovery. Operating leverage in inflationary environment. Capital-light model generates consistent dividends.

Healthcare dividend aristocrat with 51 consecutive years of increases. Diversified medical device, diagnostics, and pharma portfolio. Better positioned than pure-play semis in this environment. Dividend growth trajectory outpaces inflation. Capital preservation through cycles.

Tech dividend grower (not semiconductor-exposed like SOXL). Benefits from AI cloud infrastructure without semis cyclicality headwinds. Azure growth and AI positioning provide capital appreciation alongside dividend growth. Decoupled from semiconductor downturn affecting SOXL. 6% position captures tech upside while maintaining dividend income mandate.

Industrial conglomerate with 68 consecutive years of dividend increases. Manufacturing and infrastructure exposure benefits from potential fiscal stimulus or capex cycles. Dividend aristocrat provides yield and defensive industrial exposure. Complements healthcare/staples concentration with industrial diversification.

Energy sector ETF currently up +7.57% in portfolio, benefiting from geopolitical supply disruption (US-Iran tensions around Strait of Hormuz). Major holdings (Exxon, Chevron, ConocoPhillips) have strong dividend yields (3-5% range) and cash flow. Geopolitical tailwind for oil prices (currently $92+) provides near-term support. Tactical overweight captures energy dividend opportunity while inflation hedging.

Financial sector ETF positioned to benefit from higher interest rates (steeper yield curve increases net interest margins). Banks, insurance, and financials have strong dividend yields. Current +2.04% performance shows resilience. Fed hike scenario (Sept 18 66% probability) is tailwind for sector fundamentals. Maintains financial diversification while supporting dividend income objective.

iShares 20+ Year Treasury ETF held short as direct hedge against rising interest rates. Bond yields now at 4.79% (highest since Jan 2025) with Fed likely to hike 25bps on Sept 18 (66% probability). Duration risk is severe for long bonds. Short TLT position hedges downside risk to dividend stocks if rate shock occurs. Direct inverse exposure to rate-sensitive assets provides portfolio insurance while holding dividend longs.
